Title: Scammer posing as cop swindles woman of RM170,000
Article:
TANGKAK: An eatery assistant lost RM170,000 after falling victim to a scammer posing as a police officer who accused her of money laundering.
District police chief Superintendent Roslan Mohd Talib said the 51-year-old woman received a call from the suspect at 10.24am on July 8 and was told she was linked to illegal activities.
Roslan said the suspect then tricked the victim into making payments purportedly for investigation purposes.
"Believing the claims, the victim conducted 11 transactions into eight different accounts, suspected to be mule accounts, as instructed," he said in a statement.
He said the victim eventually realised she had been scammed and lodged a report at the Tangkak district police headquarters yesterday.
Roslan said the case is being investigated under Section 420 of the Penal Code.
"The public is advised to remain vigilant against scams and obtain information regarding such syndicates on the Commercial Crime Investigation Department's social media pages," he said.

Title: 30-year yields hit 19-year highs amid Fed doubts
Article:
SYDNEY: Yields on the US long bond hovered near 19-year highs in Asia on Thursday as markets questioned the Federal Reserve's resolve towards controlling inflation, leaving investors seeking more insurance against inflation risks.
Yields on 30-year bonds were at 5.2039 per cent, having hit their highest since mid-2007 at 5.2273 per cent late in New York trading.
The sudden sell-off came after the Fed left rates unchanged at Wednesday's policy meeting, even as three members of the Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted for an immediate hike.
In a post-meeting media conference, Fed Chair Kevin Warsh vowed to contain inflation but declined to offer any guidance on what action would be needed by the central bank.
"It seems the FOMC may be comfortable allowing the market to adjust financial conditions to balance inflation risks without an explicit contribution from the FOMC," said Elliot Clarke, head of international economics at Westpac.
"The immediate response of the market to this idea was a material steepening of the yield curve, highlighting participants' anxiety over inflation and policy uncertainty."
Thus, while 10-year yields had climbed to 4.73 per cent, yields on two-year notes held at 4.269 per cent, markedly steepening the curve.
Fed fund futures now implied around a 60 per cent chance the Fed would lift rates at its next meeting in September and had 33 basis points of tightening priced in by year-end.
The hawkish market view contrasted with Warsh's tone.
"Chairman Warsh made several dovish comments during his press conference," said David Mericle, chief US economist at Goldman Sachs. "The bond market also took today's meeting as dovish."
Warsh appeared to downplay artificial related-related price pressures while hinting that the rise in market interest rates could substitute for a rate hike, though without saying so explicitly, noted Mericle.
President Donald Trump, who hand-picked Warsh, called him "brilliant" following the Fed meeting.
"I know he'd love to see lower interest rates, but he's got a board, and it's a political board, and they want to keep rates up," Trump told reporters in the Oval Office.
Trump has made no secret of his desire to see rate cuts and repeatedly put pressure on the Fed to lower borrowing costs.
"One can debate that in time, but right now it looks unhelpful and has added to the market reaction," said Gavin Friend, a senior markets strategist at NAB.
"30-year yields jumped 11 basis points to 5.2 per cent - suggesting markets are not convinced of the Fed's conviction," he noted. "We'd add it is early days, and if Warsh is being driven in part by financial market reaction, he has a signal now."

Title: 'I'm like Sivaji the Boss,' Anwar says in Negri ceramah
Article:
SEREMBAN: Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has likened his political journey to the Tamil action film "Sivaji: The Boss", recounting how he overcame imprisonment and setbacks before becoming prime minister.
The Pakatan Harapan chairman drew the comparison during a meet-and-greet session with the Indian community here last night, recalling his early struggles when founding PKR.
"Listen, my friends. I am not young anymore. I am like Sivaji The Boss, the Tamil movie hero who was beaten, jailed, and ultimately won," he said.
Anwar recalled his early campaigning days in Seremban, acknowledging that his early support came from working-class Indian estate workers rather than "Tan Sris" who were afraid to show their faces.
Separately, Anwar announced that he will personally oversee all issues concerning the Indian community immediately, with the help of PKR vice-president Datuk Seri R. Ramanan.
He said his oversight would extend beyond the Malaysian Indian Transformation Unit (Mitra) to include citizenship matters, micro-financing schemes under Tekun and Amanah Ikhtiar Malaysia, and the Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (Sara) cash assistance programme.
Anwar urged the Indian community to support him and maintain PH's administration in Negri Sembilan.
"Don't be angry with me. I have been handcuffed, jailed, released from prison, and have become Sivaji the Boss. So it is all right.
"I will do my best. That is what I can promise. I want all Malays, Chinese, Indians, Kadazans, Dusuns and Dayaks to know that this man has suffered a lot.
"He has suffered throughout his life, for decades. There is no leader in the modern world today who has been beaten, stripped, kicked and thrown into a lock-up," he said.
Also present at the event were Ramanan, PH communications director Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil, and PKR political bureau ex-officio member Tengku Datuk Seri Zafrul Tengku Abdul Aziz.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Starbucks raises annual forecasts again as turnaround takes root
Article:
NEW YORK: Starbucks has raised its annual sales and profit forecasts for the second time, as CEO Brian Niccol's years-long turnaround efforts reignite demand at the world's largest coffee chain, sending its shares up five per cent in extended trading.
Under Niccol, the company has aimed to improve customer experience through a simplified menu and shortened wait times, fueling four straight quarters of comparable sales growth.
"We have more work to do," Niccol said in a statement on Wednesday, while finance chief Cathy Smith said the company is focused on what it can control amid a "dynamic operating environment"
The Seattle-based company forecast global same-store sales growth of near 6 per cent, above its prior forecast of about 5 per cent or above. It expects adjusted earnings per share to be between US$2.55 and US$2.65, compared with its previous forecast of US$2.25 to US$2.45.
"Starbucks has begun to experience market share stabilization in recent months, most notably with younger diners," Consumer Edge analyst Michael Gunther said.
"Consumers may be shifting dining dollars toward in-home eating but are leaving room in the budget for daily drink habits," he added. The "Back to Starbucks" strategy had been squeezing margins, as it involved heavy investments in staffing and store operations, which the company has looked to tackle with cost cuts through layoffs, office consolidation and streamlining its operations.
The company said refunds received in the quarter "largely offset" tariffs costs incurred so far this fiscal year.
The company's consolidated quarterly operating margin was 14.4 per cent in the quarter, compared with 10.1 per cent a year earlier. This helped it post adjusted earnings per share of 85 cents, compared with estimates of 66 cents.
Starbucks reported third-quarter global same-store sales growth of 7.9 per cent, which surpassed analysts' expectations of 5.7 per cent, according to data compiled by LSEG.

Title: Why Cash Flow Is King when Investing
Article:
MANY investors devote significant attention to earnings per share (EPS), revenue growth, and price- to-earnings (P/E) ratios when evaluating stocks.
While these measures are useful, none is more important than cash flow in determining the long-term financial strength and value of a company.
The famous investing maxim "Cash is king" reflects a simple truth: companies survive, grow, and reward shareholders with cash - not accounting profits.
Cash flow refers to the actual movement of cash into and out of a business.
Unlike reported profits, which are based on accounting principles and may include non-cash items or management estimates, cash flow reveals whether a company is genuinely generating money from its operations.
For long-term investors, cash flow often provides a clearer picture of business quality than earnings alone.
The first reason cash flow is so important is that it reflects the economic reality of a business.
A company may report impressive profits while struggling to collect payments from customers or carrying excessive inventories.
Since accounting profits are calculated using accrual accounting,
revenue may be recognised before cash is received, while expenses may be deferred or spread over several years.
Consequently, profits can sometimes paint an overly optimistic picture. Positive operating cash flow, however, demonstrates that customers are actually paying for the company's products or services and that the business is generating real cash.
Cash flow is also more difficult to manipulate than earnings. Management has considerable discretion in making accounting estimates relating to depreciation, provisions, impairment charges, revenue recognition, and asset valuations.
These judgments can significantly affect reported profits without changing the company's actual cash position.
Although cash flow can also be influenced by timing, it is generally much harder to artificially create sustainable operating cash flow over an extended period.
For this reason, experienced investors often compare net income with operating cash flow to identify potential earnings quality issues.
Another reason cash flow is critical is that businesses require cash to operate. Every company must pay salaries, suppliers, rent, utilities, taxes, and interest on borrowings.
Even highly profitable companies can fail if they run out of cash. History is filled with businesses that reported accounting profits shortly before experiencing severe liquidity problems because they lacked sufficient cash to meet short-term obligations.
Profit may appear on the income statement, but cash pays the bills.
Cash flow is equally important in funding future growth. Companies that consistently generate strong operating cash flow can invest in research and development, expand production capacity, acquire new businesses, develop new products and enter new markets without relying heavily on external financing.
This financial flexibility allows management to pursue opportunities during both good and difficult economic conditions.
Companies with weak cash generation often depend on bank loans or repeated equity fundraising, which may increase financial risk or dilute existing shareholders.
For income investors, cash flow is the foundation of sustainable dividends. Dividends are paid from cash, not accounting earnings.
A company may report healthy profits, but if operating cash flow is weak, maintaining dividend payments becomes increasingly difficult.
Investors therefore often examine free cash flow - the cash remaining after necessary capital expenditures - to determine whether dividends are adequately covered.
Companies with consistently growing free cash flow are generally better positioned to increase dividends over time.
Cash flow also provides valuable insight into management quality and capital allocation.
Competent management teams focus not only on increasing profits but also on converting those profits into cash.
Investors often evaluate the relationship between operating cash flow and net income over several years.
Businesses that consistently convert a high proportion of earnings into cash typically possess stronger competitive advantages, better working capital management, and superior operational discipline.
In addition, cash flow serves as a vital measure during periods of economic uncertainty.
During recessions or industry downturns, companies with substantial cash generation and healthy cash reserves are better equipped to withstand declining sales, supply chain disruptions, and rising borrowing costs.
They can continue investing while weaker competitors struggle to survive. Such resilience often allows financially strong companies to emerge from downturns with greater market share.
Cash flow is also central to company valuation. Professional investors frequently use discounted cash flow (DCF) analysis, which estimates the intrinsic value of a business based on its expected future free cash flows.
Unlike valuation methods that rely solely on earnings multiples, DCF focuses directly on the cash that owners can ultimately receive from the business.
Since the value of any investment depends on the future cash it can generate, cash flow naturally becomes the primary driver of intrinsic value.
Investors should therefore pay close attention to several key cash flow indicators, including operating cash flow, free cash flow, cash conversion, capital expenditure requirements and the consistency of cash generation over multiple years.
A business that regularly produces strong and growing cash flow often possesses durable competitive advantages and a healthier financial position
than one that merely reports attractive accounting profits.
In conclusion, while earnings, revenue growth, and valuation ratios remain important, cash flow provides the most reliable measure of a company's true financial health.
It reveals whether profits are genuine, determines the ability to fund operations and growth, supports dividends and strengthens resilience during economic downturns, and forms the basis of intrinsic valuation.
As Warren Buffett has often emphasised, investing is ultimately about buying businesses that will generate cash for their owners over time. For prudent investors seeking long-term wealth creation, consistently strong cash flow should remain one of the most important criteria in stock selection.

Title: Chinese carmakers piling pressure on UK rivals, auto industry chief says
Article:
LONDON: A wave of Chinese entrants into Britain's car market is piling pressure on traditional manufacturers, forcing them to offer deeper discounts to compete with lower-cost imports, the head of the country's main automotive industry body said on Thursday.
Chinese brands have rapidly expanded their presence in Britain in recent years, winning market share with competitively priced electric and plug-in hybrid models and intensifying competition for established automakers.
"In terms of the volume, they're under extraordinary pressure because the Chinese can produce good vehicles at a cheaper cost," the Society of Motor Manufacturers and Traders CEO ​Mike Hawes told reporters at a briefing on Thursday.
"There's a lot of discounting going on in the market ... That's basically to try and compete with a Chinese brand," he said.
Chinese-owned brands now account for about 15 per cent of UK new car registrations, according to SMMT data, led by SAIC Motor's MG, BYD and Chery's JAECOO and OMODA brands.
Hawes said increased competition was one of several factors behind the contraction in British vehicle manufacturing, which fell 7.5 per cent in the first half of 2026 as trade uncertainty and lower investment also weighed on production.
Across Europe, automakers have been grappling with intensifying competition from Chinese rivals. Last week, Germany's Volkswagen said it would deepen cost cuts to remain competitive against Chinese brands.
That was despite the European Union imposing tariffs on Chinese-built electric vehicles in 2024 after concluding they benefited from unfair state subsidies.
Britain, which left the bloc in 2020, has not introduced similar tariffs. Hawes said any investigation into Chinese imports would need to be triggered by complaints from UK manufacturers, adding that, to his knowledge, none had been made.
He said Chinese competition was just one of several pressures facing Britain's automotive industry, highlighting also high energy costs, weak investment and regulation.

Title: Salman Rushdie stabbing: Assailant convicted of terrorism, faces life sentence
Article:
NEW YORK: A federal jury on Wednesday convicted novelist Salman Rushdie's assailant of "engaging in an act of terrorism" for the bloody August 2022 attack at a New York cultural centre.
Hadi Matar, a 28-year-old Lebanese American, "chose to align his values with the terroristic values of the leaders of Iran," said US Attorney Michael DiGiacomo, adding the defendant spent months planning the stabbing that nearly killed Rushdie and left him blind in one eye.
Matar was also convicted of supporting the Iran-backed Lebanese group Hizbollah, after investigators found materials from the organisation at his home.
Federal prosecutors said Matar followed a fatwa calling for Rushdie's execution, first issued in 1989 by the late Iranian leader Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini, for fictionalising the Prophet Muhammad in his bestselling book, "The Satanic Verses."
The fatwa was reaffirmed in 2017 by Iran's late Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei, and endorsed in a 2006 speech by Hizbollah leader Hassan Nasrallah, prosecutors said.
"His brutal attack on Mr Rushdie during a peaceful speaking event is a chilling reminder of the global reach of Iranian terrorism," DiGiacomo said.
The attack took place at the Chautauqua Institution in Mayville, New York, during a free speech conference, where then-24-year-old Matar leapt onto the stage and stabbed Rushdie repeatedly with a six-inch blade.
Matar was already convicted of attempted murder and sentenced to 25 years in prison by the New York state justice system, and now faces an additional maximum federal penalty of life in prison.
He is due for sentencing Nov 3.
Matar told a reporter before his trials that he believed Rushdie had "attacked Islam."
Rushdie lived in seclusion in London for a decade after the 1989 fatwa, but for the past 20 years – until the attack – lived relatively normally in New York.
In 2026, Rushdie said violence is the tool of "the unscrupulous using the ignorant" to attack culture.
"For the authoritarian, culture is the enemy. Whether that's journalism or universities or music or writing," Rushdie said. "The uncultured and ignorant, and the radical don't like it, and they take steps against it, which we see every day."--AFP

Title: Wall Street closes down sharply after Fed holds rates unchanged
Article:
NEW YORK: Wall Street ended sharply lower on Wednesday after the Federal Reserve held interest rates steady, with AI-related chip stocks adding to recent declines ahead of quarterly reports from Microsoft and Meta Platforms and the Nasdaq 100 index marking an 11 per cent drop from its June record high.
The Fed's widely expected decision to leave the benchmark interest rate in the 3.50 per cent-3.75 per cent range drew dissents from three of the 12 members of the policy-setting Federal Open Market Committee who "preferred" a quarter-percentage-point hike at this meeting.
The benchmark S&P 500 hit its lowest level in a month, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite index was down about 9 per cent from its June record high.
The Nasdaq 100 index dropped 2.1 per cent, extending recent losses as investors unloaded AI-related stocks due to ongoing concerns about heavy capital spending. That index is composed of the Nasdaq exchange's most valuable non-financial companies.
Investors had mostly expected the Fed to keep rates unchanged. Inflation has been running above the central bank's target for more than five years, and up until last month it was accelerating as the war in the Middle East pushed up global fuel and food prices.
"The Fed held pat, as expected. The bigger question now though becomes, how much pressure will they have to hike in September? Inflation is running hot and with surging crude oil, the market expects the next hike to indeed be in September," said Ryan Detrick, chief market strategist at Carson Group.
nvestors worry that major US companies are deepening a web of AI-linked investments and continuing to funnel billions into the emerging technology at the expense of free cash flow.
Meta Platforms dropped four per cent in extended trade after the social media company said it now expects 2026 capital expenditure to be between US$130 billion and US$145 billion, compared with its prior forecast of US$125 billion to US$145 billion.
Also after the bell, Microsoft climbed 0.6 per cent after it topped Wall Street estimates for quarterly cloud revenue growth, a sign its massive spending on AI infrastructure was paying off.
Meanwhile, competition from China has been heating up, both in the race to develop advanced chips and as Chinese firms roll out cheaper AI models.
Speaking to reporters, Fed chief Kevin Warsh said spending on AI was laying the groundwork for future growth.
AI-related chipmakers added to recent losses after a sixfold jump in SK Hynix's quarterly profit fell short of lofty investor expectations. The South Korean company's shares fell 10 per cent.
AI infrastructure company Vertiv slumped 17 per cent after missing quarterly revenue expectations. The S&P 500 declined 1.52 per cent to end the session at 7,316.15 points.
The Nasdaq declined 1.74 per cent to 24,442.94 points, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average declined 2.19 per cent to 51,594.14 points. Eight of the 11 S&P 500 sector indexes declined, led lower by industrials, down 3.24 per cent, followed by a 2.5 per cent loss in information technology.
Analysts on average expect S&P 500 aggregate second-quarter earnings to jump 40 per cent from a year ago, with AI-related stocks accounting for much of that growth, according to LSEG I/B/E/S.
Strong earnings forecasts and Wall Street's recent decline have left the S&P 500 trading at about 20 times expected earnings, just above its 10-year average of 19, according to LSEG data.
Ford Motor gained 2.1 per cent after raising its annual profit outlook for a second time this year. Lennox tumbled 21 per cent after the HVAC solutions maker lowered its annual profit forecast.
Visa rose 0.6 per cent after the company beat estimates for quarterly profit, helped by World Cup-fueled travel demand. Declining stocks outnumbered rising ones within the S&P 500 by a 1.8-to-one ratio.
The S&P 500 posted 32 new highs and four new lows; the Nasdaq recorded 121 new highs and 230 new lows.
Volume on US exchanges was relatively heavy, with 17.7 billion shares traded, compared to an average of 17.3 billion shares over the previous 20 sessions.

Title: Bolivia prosecutor orders arrest of ex-leader Morales over protests
Article:
LA PAZ, (Bolivia): Bolivian prosecutors on Wednesday issued an arrest warrant for former socialist president Evo Morales, accusing him of fomenting recent protests that paralysed the country.
Enormous anti-government demonstrations choked the Andean nation in May and June, causing severe fuel, food and medicine shortages in some cities.
The movement started with workers and Indigenous communities voicing their grievances over Bolivia's worst economic crisis in decades.
But protests escalated to demand the resignation of US-backed President Rodrigo Paz, who has accused Morales of orchestrating the unrest.
Wednesday's warrant was related to an investigation into dozens of roadblocks erected during that period, Attorney General Roger Mariaca said.
The probe stemmed from an "armed uprising" and "terrorism" complaint filed by a right-wing conglomerate of civic leaders and businesses against Morales, trade unionist Mario Argollo and Indigenous figure Vicente Salazar.
A section of the government later joined the complaint.
The president has also accused Morales, who hails from the coca-growing Chapare region, of drug trafficking — without providing evidence.
Morales, Bolivia's first-ever Indigenous leader, is in hiding in his political stronghold Chapare to escape separate charges of trafficking a minor.
He is accused of having relations with a 15-year-old girl, with whom he is alleged to have fathered a child while in power.
The teenager's parents allegedly consented to the relationship in exchange for benefits. Morales denies the allegations.
Paz previously said he was planning an operation in the former president's political bastion, without specifying when.
The conservative leader managed to quell public unrest by declaring a state of emergency in June, allowing him to deploy the army and outlaw demonstrations.
He took office last year on a promise to revive the economy after two decades of socialist rule.
His cost-cutting program has however run into stiff opposition from trade unions, farmers and Indigenous organisations.
Morales believes Paz's neoliberal policies are "stoking a civil war," he told AFP in an interview in June.
"There is no reason to intervene," he said of a potential government operation in Chapare. — AFP

Title: New corporate champions, new-age banking
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia risks struggling to produce its next generation of corporate champions unless the financial sector takes a more forward-looking approach to risk, innovation and entrepreneurship, industry leaders said.
At the same time, Islamic banks risk losing relevance among younger customers if they fail to match expectations for seamless, customer-focused digital banking.
They noted that a more forward-looking approach to financing innovation and entrepreneurship is needed to help build high-growth companies that will drive Malaysia's future economy.
CelcomDigi Bhd chairman Tengku Datuk Seri Azmil Zahruddin Raja Abdul Aziz said Malaysia's largest listed companies have remained largely unchanged over the past two decades, highlighting the need to nurture more emerging businesses.
"If you look at the largest 30 companies on the stock exchange today versus 10-20 years ago, it's by and large the same companies. Nothing much has changed," he said.
Azmil was speaking at a panel session on "Finance For A Flourishing Society: Propelling Malaysia's Long-term Aspirations" at the Sasana Symposium 2026.
He said Malaysia has excelled in financing large infrastructure projects but has been less successful in supporting startups and other high-growth businesses.
"As a sector, we are very good at infrastructure financing, where you have large upfront investments and returns over a long period. But when it comes to higher-risk, more failure-prone startups and industries that require a different risk appetite, I think we're doing quite poorly overall."
Azmil said financing innovation requires financial institutions to accept that not every investment will succeed.
"You have to be willing to take that risk. When you're trying something new, such as developing a new algorithm, you're probably going to have a high failure rate.
"But you have to ring-fence that, so you know how much risk you're taking and how much you can afford to take," he said.
He added that larger financial institutions are better placed to pioneer such lending models because they have stronger capital buffers and can absorb losses while building expertise in assessing emerging businesses.
EY Malaysia managing partner Datuk Abdul Rauf Rashid said the financial sector must also adapt to an economy increasingly driven by innovation, technology and intellectual property.
"The world's largest companies today are no longer defined by tangible assets. A significant portion of their value comes from intellectual property, organisational capabilities and data," he said.
Younger Customers Want Simplicity
Bank Islam Malaysia Bhd chief executive officer Raja Teh Maimunah Raja Abdul Aziz said banks should focus on delivering customer-centric digital services rather than emphasising the complexity of products behind the scenes.
"I have to caution everybody when it comes to serving the younger generation going forward. I can tell you today, nobody cares about what contract you use. Customer centricity is everything," she said.
Raja Teh Maimunah was speaking at a panel session titled "From Policy to People: Strengthening the Impact of Islamic Finance" at the symposium.
The session was moderated by the central bank's Islamic finance department director Nurul Izza Idris and featured deputy governor Adnan Zaylani Mohamed Zahid and Yayasan Hasanah managing director and trustee Siti Kamariah Ahmad Subki.
Raja Teh Maimunah cautioned that Islamic banks could lose customers seeking Syariah-compliant financial services if their digital offerings become cumbersome or fail to meet rising expectations.
"My fear is that if you get caught up with whatever's in the back end and our delivery becomes frictional, then you will lose people who believe in it," she said.
She said customer experience had become the defining factor for younger consumers, who expect fast, seamless and intuitive digital services.
"If we don't focus on customer delivery, we will lose relevance. Today, it's all about instant gratification. Digitisation is not something you should still be fearful of or not understand, especially when it comes to artificial intelligence," she said.
Raja Teh Maimunah added that many senior decision-makers may not fully understand the expectations of younger customers, whose banking preferences are driven by speed and ease of use.
"Your customers are much younger than you. You may not understand what they're looking for," she said.
Touch 'n Go Shows The Way
Raja Teh Maimunah cited the widespread adoption of Touch 'n Go eWallet as evidence that consumers choose financial services based on convenience rather than the technology or contractual structures behind them.
"Why has Touch 'n Go grown by leaps and bounds? Because it's easy to use. They don't ask you how your back-end engineering works. They don't ask what kind of contracts you use.
"As Islamic finance practitioners, we have to make sure everything is Syariah compliant. That is our job. Don't burden customers with questions about whether one contract is better than another. If it's halal, go for it. Just make sure it's frictionless.
"If you fall behind, younger users will simply choose something else, and it may not be Syariah compliant because all they want today is instant delivery," she said.
Raja Teh Maimunah also called on Islamic financial institutions to strengthen their digital capabilities by recruiting talent from outside the Islamic finance ecosystem where necessary.
She acknowledged that younger, digitally savvy customers are increasingly questioning the value proposition of Islamic finance when pricing and customer experience appear similar to those of conventional banks.
"If you don't have the talent within the Islamic finance ecosystem itself, you have to employ people from outside your ecosystem," she said.
"For as long as Islamic financial institutions operate within a fractional banking system, we still have liquidity ratios and capital ratios governed by Basel standards.
Meanwhile, Malaysian International Chamber of Commerce and Industry vice president Datuk Azman Shah Mohd Yusof said financing should increasingly support investments that enhance productivity and competitiveness, even if returns take longer to materialise.
"Some investments take longer to deliver returns, but they are necessary because the multiplier effect is there," he said.

Title: Maju Junction assets up for auction with RM353.95mil reserve price
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Maju Junction, which has stood at the intersection of Jalan Sultan Ismail and Jalan Tuanku Abdul Rahman for more than two decades, is set to see some of its properties up for auction next month.
A total of 38 strata parcels in the office and retail complex, registered under ASM Properties Sdn Bhd, are set to go under the hammer via e-Lelong on Aug 20 at a reserve price of RM353.95 million.
The properties comprise office, commercial and car park lots, with the successful bidder required to pay a 10 per cent deposit and settle the balance purchase price within 120 days.
The auction follows execution proceedings involving Perwaja Terengganu Sdn Bhd as plaintiff and ASM Properties as defendant, according to the proclamation of sale issued by the High Court of Malaya here.
According to the proclamation of sale, the auction is being conducted pursuant to an order for sale dated June 20, 2025, and a subsequent court order dated June 23, 2026.
The proceedings were initiated under Sections 256 and 257 of the National Land Code 1965 and Order 83 of the Rules of Court 2012.
RM198mil Judgment In Background
Court records show that Perwaja Terengganu and Maju Holdings Sdn Bhd were previously embroiled in litigation arising from agreements linked to the privatisation of the Perwaja Group.
On July 25, 2019, the High Court entered judgment in favour of Perwaja, ordering Maju Holdings to pay RM197.99 million, together with interest.
Maju Holdings subsequently appealed, but the Court of Appeal dismissed the appeal on Dec 20, 2022, upholding the High Court's decision.
However, the court documents seen by Business Times do not establish whether the execution proceedings involving ASM Properties arose directly from the earlier judgment against Maju Holdings or from a separate legal basis.
Business Times contacted Md Tajuddin & Co, solicitors acting for Perwaja, to seek clarification on the basis of the execution proceedings and whether they were connected to the earlier litigation involving Maju Holdings.
A representative of the firm declined to comment.

Title: Affordable housing vital for long-term economic stability
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Affordable  housing programmes are more than a way to bridge the housing affordability gap— they also help young Malaysians build wealth, improve social mobility and achieve long-term economic stability.
Universiti Teknologi Malaysia Associate Professor (property economics) Dr Muhammad Najib Razali said state housing schemes such as Rumah Selangorku  help address market gaps, as private developers often focus on higher-profit segments beyond the reach of many low- and middle-income households.
"These programmes also support asset-based welfare theory, which views homeownership as a mechanism for wealth accumulation, financial security and long-term social mobility. By enabling young households to own homes earlier, these schemes contribute to broader economic and social stability."
Najib  said such programmes promoted community stability and  sustainable urban growth .
He added that future policies should move beyond selling cheaper homes  to integrating housing with jobs, public transport, healthcare, education and commercial facilities, in line with the concept of transit-oriented development (TOD) and the 15-minute city.
"When homes are well connected to jobs and essential services, affordability is determined not only by the purchase price but also by the total cost of living.
"Ultimately, sustainability depends on a balanced framework in which the government, developers, financial institutions and local authorities share responsibility," he said.
He pointed to South Korea as  a benchmark, where there is  sustained  affordable housing through strong government support, public-private partnerships, strategic land development and financing assistance for first-time buyers despite rapid urbanisation.
"Affordable housing is most effective when governments balance affordability with sufficient incentives for developers."
Universiti Teknologi Mara's Centre of Studies in Real Estate Associate Professor Dr Rohayu Abdul Majid said such programmes acted as a vital socioeconomic stabiliser for young Malaysians entering the urban workforce.
"A fresh graduate or young professional earning between RM3,000 and RM5,000 a month experiences severe affordability mismatch as modern, well-connected family homes often start above RM500,000.
"Programmes such as Rumah Selangorku and Residensi Wilayah (Rumawip) bridge this gap through strict price caps, allowing young households to invest in homeownership instead of renting."
She added that  such programmes also help keep young workers connected to employment centres and essential services.
Rohayu said future improvements should address the hidden costs,  such as maintenance charges and sinking fund contributions, while calling for greater emphasis on government-backed rent-to-own programmes, particularly those who are not ready for 30- to 35-year housing loans.
Location and connectivity remain key determinants of true affordability.
"A cheap home can become expensive if residents have to spend on transportation because of poor access to public transport.
"Future developments under programmes  such as Rumah Selangorku and Rumawip must be closely integrated with mass rapid transit,  light rail transit or feeder bus routes to reduce overall living costs," she said.

Title: Putrajaya wants federal, state housing schemes to complement each other
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Putrajaya  aims to create an ecosystem where federal and state affordable housing schemes complement rather than compete with one another.
The government said raising  the homeownership rate would require a coordinated approach combining affordable housing supply, easier financing, policy reforms and closer collaboration among the federal and state governments, financial institutions and the private sector.
Deputy Housing and Local Government Minister Datuk Aiman Athirah Sabu said this approach would enable more Malaysians to buy homes that matched their preferred location, budget and financial capacity.
She said schemes  such as Residensi Wilayah and Rumah Selangorku played a vital role in expanding homeownership, particularly among first-time buyers, young people, and low- and middle-income households.
"The federal government is responsible for formulating policies, establishing the legal
framework and providing various incentives, while state governments tailor housing supply according to local needs, affordability and market conditions."
Aiman said the federal government was also introducing financing initiatives to help homebuyers secure loans, including the Housing Credit Guarantee Scheme, which provided guarantees of up to RM500,000 for first-home purchases.
She added that housing reforms under the National Housing Policy 2026-2035 focused on strengthening collaboration with state governments and the private sector,  including optimising government land, adopting innovative development models such as joint ventures, cross-subsidisation and land swaps, as well as expanding financing options.
[[nid:1500054]]
"The government's goal is not merely to build more homes but to ensure they are genuinely affordable, strategically located and able to meet the needs of the people."
Other initiatives to support buyers include the People's Residences Programme, Rumah Mesra Rakyat and PR1MA housing.
She acknowledged that the challenges facing young Malaysians extended beyond rising house prices, with slower income growth, higher living costs and financing difficulties also affecting homeownership.
"Housing sector reforms under the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP) will focus on more comprehensive and sustainable solutions, reflecting the government's commitment to building a sustainable housing ecosystem where more young people and first-time homebuyers can not only afford to buy homes but also sustain homeownership over the long term," she said.
Malaysia's homeownership rate stood at 76.5 per cent as of February. Under the 13MP, one million affordable homes are to be built between 2026 and 2035 through a collaborative effort involving the federal and state governments, and private developers.
Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming previously said housing policies under the 13MP were guided by principles of liveability, sustainability, affordability, connectivity and community building, with humanity at the centre of policymaking.

Title: Homeownership: Opening doors for young Malaysians
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Soaring property prices and the rising cost of living have pushed homeownership beyond the reach of many young Malaysians.
Affordable housing schemes, however, are helping to bridge that gap by making it easier for first-time buyers to get on the property ladder, with some able to own homes by paying a deposit as low as RM500 or, in some cases, none at all.
Various government initiatives have eased one of the biggest barriers to homeownership by reducing the hefty upfront costs typically associated with buying a property.
Unlike homes on the open market, where buyers need tens of thousands of ringgit for the down payment, affordable housing programmes provide a more accessible pathway for young Malaysians to own a home and build long-term financial security, particularly in the Klang Valley.
Norman Arifin, 32, bought an apartment in Cyberjaya for RM288,000  under the Rumah Selangorku scheme two years ago without having to pay a deposit.
The sales manager, who earns about RM6,000 monthly, said the affordable pricing for the partially furnished apartment made the scheme an attractive option.
"Without the Rumah Selangorku scheme, it would have been almost impossible for me to own a home at a young age," he added.
Assistant executive Aqilah Hashim, 27, who earns RM3,000 monthly, said she managed to buy a RM232,000 apartment under the Rumah Selangorku scheme with a RM500 deposit.
"I bought a home because I wanted to own an asset. The affordable housing scheme helped me achieve that goal without placing too much financial pressure on me," she said.
Aqilah added that the affordable housing scheme accelerated her homeownership journey as its eligibility requirements were more attainable for working individuals.
While government housing schemes have lowered the barriers to homeownership, young buyers entering the open market continue to face substantially higher upfront costs.
Danial Ahmad Rosli, 25, who bought a RM556,000 condominium unit as an investment property, had to prepare a RM56,000 down payment after securing a RM500,000 loan.
The site engineer, who earns about RM8,000 a month, said the upfront payment was made possible with financial assistance from his family. He covers the monthly loan repayments himself.
"I thank my family for helping with the down payment because it would have been impossible to raise that amount on my own."
Alisya Syukor, 24, purchased a RM500,000 double-storey subsale house after preparing for homeownership since her university days.
She saved for the RM25,000 down payment over four years by cutting expenses, including staying with her family and commuting between Tanjung Malim and Kuala Lumpur.
"I started saving after finishing school and continued saving consistently after I started working.
"My family's encouragement and my own financial planning motivated me to prepare for future commitments, including starting a family," she said.
SUGGESTIONS FOR FUTURE HOUSING POLICIES
Norman said banks could improve the home-buying process by speeding up loan assessments and approvals to reduce waiting times for buyers.
He said more affordable housing projects should be developed in strategic locations with better access to public transport, workplaces, schools and essential amenities.
"These steps will make owning a home much easier and more practical, especially for young people," he said.
Aqilah called on the government to extend stamp duty exemptions for first-time homebuyers and streamline the exemption process, particularly for individuals who inherited family land but had never purchased a property.

Title: Negri Sembilan polls: Status quo tested as race heats up
Article:
THE Negri Sembilan  election has emerged as an electoral battleground where the Barisan Nasional-Perikatan Nasional  alliance is perceived not only as a credible challenger, but also as having a realistic pathway towards forming the next state government.
Following BN's commanding performance in Johor and the perceived weakening of Pakatan Harapan  in several rural and semi-urban constituencies, political momentum appears to be shifting.
Although DAP continues to retain several established strong-holds, recent political trends are widely interpreted by BN-PN supporters as  fractures in PH's support that could be strategically exploited.
The official results of the 2023 Negri Sembilan election provide the essential baseline for understanding the present contest.
PH secured 17 seats, including all 11 contested by DAP, while BN won 14 seats and PN obtained five.
However, many PH victories were achieved with relatively narrow margins, particularly in mixed and suburban constituencies.
Consequently, numerous seats cannot realistically be described as completely secure.
Instead, they remain marginal constituencies that may prove highly sensitive to shifts in Malay voting patterns and changes among undecided voters.
Johor's recent election has strengthened confidence within BN that support is recovering.
BN captured 48 of the southern  state's 56 seats while PH secured only eight.
MALAY VOTER CONSOLIDATION
Although Johor possesses unique historical and organisational characteristics that had contributed to the outcome, one  observation remains: Malay voter support appeared to consolidate behind BN, while urban support alone proved insufficient to sustain PH's dominance.
BN supporters believe  similar  dynamics could emerge in Negri Sembilan.
Sabah is also cited by proponents of this assessment as reinforcing another important political narrative.
They argue that PH and DAP are no longer  invulnerable, even in constituencies once considered  secure.
Although Sabah's political environment differs substantially from Peninsular Malaysia, they contend that voters have become increasingly pragmatic
From this perspective, BN-PN may find greater opportunities to compete in constituencies previously regarded as difficult.
Within Negri Sembilan itself, supporters of BN-PN frequently identify between five and eight constituencies as realistically competitive. They further argue that  coordination between BN and PN in direct contests  increases the probability of victory.
AVOIDING SPLIT VOTES
The BN-PN electoral understanding has also altered the competitive landscape.
BN is contesting 25 seats while PN is contesting 11,  avoiding opposition vote splitting that occurred in earlier elections.
Advocates of the alliance view this arrangement as providing a clear  advantage as Malay votes are less likely to fragment, while PH is perceived as relying more heavily upon urban and non-Malay support in several rural and semi-urban constituencies.
In many marginal seats, previous victory margins measured only several hundred votes, suggesting that relatively modest electoral movement could alter constituency outcomes.
Negri Sembilan's demographic composition also contributes to expectations of an intensely competitive election.
While Bumiputera voters constitute the majority, Chinese and Indian communities remain significant, particularly within urban centres.
Nevertheless, BN-PN supporters contend that PH's urban margins have narrowed while economic concerns have streng-thened BN-PN's position in suburban constituencies.
For BN, the perceived opportunity rests upon three principal factors: consolidated Malay support, credible local candidates  and a stability narrative strengthened after Johor.
Umno is widely viewed by its supporters as regaining organisational momentum, while cooperation with PN is regarded as reinforcing the conservative vote.
MCA and MIC are expected to retain sufficient non-Malay support to remain competitive in mixed constituencies.
Meanwhile, PH and DAP face the challenge of defending increasingly competitive seats.
Although they continue to enjoy significant urban support, issues surrounding living costs, perceptions of government performance and political fatigue after successive electoral cycles are regarded by critics as increasing electoral pressure.
INTENSIFYING COMPETITION
Three broad scenarios are commonly discussed.
First, BN-PN could  form the state government should continued Malay voter consolidation enable the alliance to capture several marginal seats.
Second, a closely divided assembly could emerge if PH retains urban constituencies while  losing suburban areas.
Third, PH could remain in government through  strong mobilisation across mixed constituencies.
Ultimately, the Negri Sembilan election is  viewed as extending beyond the defence of the status quo.  Nevertheless, the final outcome depends on   polling day itself, and only the official vote will determine whether current political expectations translate into electoral reality.
* The writer is a political and economic analyst

Title: Firefighting helicopter crash kills seven in Argentina
Article:
BUENOS AIRES: Seven people died when a firefighting helicopter in Argentina's western San Juan province crashed on Wednesday, a local official said.
The Bell 412 aircraft had been training before heading to a neighbouring province to help put out days-long fires when it crashed in Ischigualasto natural park.
It lost contact with base on Wednesday morning at around 10.30 am (1330 GMT).
"With profound sorrow, we received the news of the helicopter accident that occurred in our province, in which seven people sadly lost their lives," San Juan Governor Marcelo Orrego wrote on X.
Fatalities included firefighters, police officers and civil protection personnel, he said.
The causes of the accident were under investigation and a rescue team had been deployed, emergency services stated.
Argentine Security Minister Alejandra Monteoliva expressed her condolences on X.
"I stand with each of the families and their fellow officers in this moment of profound grief," she wrote.
A local journalist and friend of one of the victims, police officer German Videla, told TN television channel that the pair had been in contact about an hour before the crash.
The helicopter "shattered into a thousand pieces. It's shocking," said journalist Mauricio Davila, who had also spoken with rescue teams at the crash site.
San Juan's local government declared three days of mourning following the accident, during which the national and provincial flags will be flown at half-mast.
La Rioja, a semi-arid region roughly the size of Austria, has been grappling with several forest fires in mountainous areas since the beginning of the week.
Hundreds of hectares have burned in just three days, local firefighters told AFP.--AFP

Title: MyIMMs breach a national security issue, not just cybercrime, says criminologist [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The alleged hacking and manipulation of the Malaysian Immigration System (MyIMMs) should be treated as a national security issue rather than merely a corruption or cybercrime case.
Senior criminologist Datuk Dr P. Sundramoorthy said the Immigration Department serves as Malaysia's first line of defence, making any compromise of the MyIMMs platform a direct threat to the country's border security and sovereignty.
"MyIMMs is not merely an administrative database. It is critical national security infrastructure that regulates the entry, movement and exit of foreign nationals.
"If allegations that the system was deliberately manipulated are proven, this represents a compromise of Malaysia's border security architecture rather than simply an IT breach," he told the New Straits Times.
Sundramoorthy said the case also highlighted the dangerous convergence between organised crime and insider corruption, noting that criminal syndicates rarely succeed without assistance from individuals entrusted with legitimate authority and system access.
He was commenting on the arrest of 12 people, including four Immigration officers, who hacked the MyIMMs to fraudulently process and approve Temporary Employment Visit Passes (PLKS).
Initial investigations revealed that the syndicate had exploited unused PLKS quotas dating back to 2011 to issue work passes without paying the required levy.
"When trusted public officers collaborate with criminal organisations, they become trusted facilitators who enable illegal activities to appear legitimate.
"Such partnerships allow syndicates to bypass security controls that would otherwise be extremely difficult to penetrate."
He warned that vulnerabilities within the immigration system could facilitate human trafficking, migrant smuggling, labour exploitation, money laundering, document fraud and other forms of transnational organised crime.
Sundramoorthy said the incident should not be viewed solely as a cybersecurity failure but as a governance issue involving insider corruption, weak oversight and technological vulnerabilities.
"Technology itself is rarely the weakest link. Even the most sophisticated digital systems become vulnerable when individuals entrusted with access abuse their authority.
"Insider threats often pose greater risks than external hackers because insiders already possess authorised access and understand institutional procedures."
Sundramoorthy urged the authorities to conduct a comprehensive forensic audit of the MyIMMs system, review all privileged user accounts, verify work passes issued during the suspected period of compromise, strengthen AI-driven monitoring and establish a multi-agency task force involving the Immigration Department, police, the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission, the National Cyber Security Agency, the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission and independent cybersecurity experts.
He said long-term reforms should include stricter access controls, dual authorisation for sensitive transactions, regular integrity audits, staff rotation and continuous background screening for officers handling critical national databases.
"If the allegations are ultimately proven in court and public officers knowingly collaborated with organised criminal syndicates to compromise a critical national security system, their actions represent a profound betrayal of public trust and the nation's sovereignty.
"Parliament should also review whether existing laws are adequate to deal with such grave offences," he added.

Title: Death toll rises to 13 as rescuers search Japan quake rubble
Article:
KUMAMOTO: Rescuers battled through the tangled wreckage of a Japanese shopping mall Wednesday searching for any trapped survivors after a strong earthquake killed at least 13 people.
A massive explosion ripped through the mall around 50 minutes after the 7.1-magnitude tremor on Tuesday in the southwestern Kumamoto region, where in 2016 twin quakes killed nearly 300 people.
Tuesday's tremor caused widespread damage on the island of Kyushu, flattening homes, triggering fires and leaving tens of thousands of residents without power and water.
Several aftershocks have rattled the area since the initial quake.
Akio Yoshida, the president of mall operator Aeon, said three people died at the facility in the town of Kashima, with one more fatality feared and three others missing.
"The cause is still being investigated, but it's likely that gas caused it," fellow Aeon executive Keiji Ohno told a news conference where he and others bowed in apology.
Five people were also confirmed killed and four others were unaccounted for at the Nippon Paper Industries factory in Yatsushiro city, where part of a red-and-white smokestack collapsed, a government official told AFP.
"Extensive damage has been confirmed, including casualties, collapsed buildings, fires and damage to roads," Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said in Tokyo as she announced 13 fatalities, describing a "race against time" to help those affected.
Government spokesman Minoru Kihara said that as of early Wednesday more than 9,000 people had sought refuge in 506 shelters in three regions of Kyushu island.
Around 130 police, 450 firefighters and 170 military personnel were involved in the rescue operation at the Aeon Mall Kumamoto, he said.
Some stunned locals said the quake was the biggest they had felt in their lifetimes, measuring at the top of Japan's seven-level shindo scale of shakiness.
"It was the strongest quake I ever experienced," Kanzo Matsumoto, 73, the operator of a luxury onsen hot spring inn in Yatsushiro, told AFP.
Japan's Geospatial Information Authority said some ground surfaces were displaced by as much as 87cm in the quake, Jiji Press reported.
- 'THEN AN EXPLOSION' -
Tokito Kitagawa, 21, pulled over at a convenience store when the quake struck as he was travelling in Kumamoto on his motorcycle.
"There was a sudden big noise," Kitagawa told AFP. "I couldn't stay standing. I had to crouch down. Then all the cup noodles fell all over me on the floor."
One user on X who said that they worked inside the mall recounted the moments after the quake hit.
The user with the handle Palan said staff had guided customers outside and then some employees went back to get their belongings.
"Since there didn't seem to be any smoke inside the premises from what we could see, we felt reassured," they said. "Then an explosion occurred."
Footage from inside the mall showed rescue workers in orange overalls and white helmets picking their way through a mass of twisted steel, dangling cables and chunks of ceiling.
Initial reports had said that as many as 20 to 30 people were trapped inside.
Some 31,200 households and facilities still had no power on Wednesday morning, while 84,000 homes were suffering water disruptions, officials said.
TV footage showed people queueing for petrol and drinking water.
- TRAINS SUSPENDED -
The powerful tremor, which struck at 4.27pm (0727 GMT) on Tuesday, knocked over a cargo train, flattened a traditional "torii" gateway and cracked roads, making many impassable.
High-speed shinkansen trains mostly remained suspended on Wednesday.
Footage also showed parts of a wall at the centuries-old Kumamoto Castle collapsing.
The US Geological Survey measured the quake at 6.8, lower than Japan's reading of 7.1.
Japan is one of the world's most seismically active countries, sitting on top of four major tectonic plates along the western edge of the Pacific "Ring of Fire."
Kumamoto was hit by two devastating earthquakes in 2016, which killed 273 people and injured more than 2,800.
The archipelago, home to around 125 million people, typically experiences hundreds of jolts every year and accounts for about 18 per cent of the world's earthquakes.
The vast majority are mild, although the damage they cause varies according to their location and the depth below the Earth's surface at which they strike.
Japan is haunted by the memory of a massive 9.0-magnitude undersea quake in 2011, which triggered a tsunami that killed or left missing around 18,500 people and wrecked the Fukushima nuclear plant.--AFP

Title: Microsoft tops forecasts as cloud, AI drive US$90b revenue
Article:
SAN FRANCISCO: Microsoft beat analysts' expectations in its latest quarterly report, saying Wednesday that the results were partly driven by its cloud and artificial intelligence divisions.
The tech giant reported US$90 billion in revenue and US$35.8 billion in net income in the last quarter of its fiscal year which ended in June, potentially alleviating concerns from investors and analysts about whether its investments in AI are paying off.
Its AI-powered business productivity tool, called Copilot, also has over 30 million paid users which shows "confidence" from customers as they use Microsoft to "power their AI transformation," CEO Satya Nadella said in a statement.
Microsoft also saw a US$3.2 billion gain from its investment in Anthropic, the company said.
Its investments in OpenAI boosted Microsoft's net profit by US$480 million in its fourth quarter and US$4.9 billion for its full fiscal year, the company added.
Major tech companies in the United States have been spending billions to build out AI infrastructure and develop increasingly more advanced AI models.
Amazon, Microsoft, Alphabet and Meta are collectively on track to pour roughly US$700 billion into AI data centers, chips and computing infrastructure this year alone.
In June, Google parent company Alphabet announced it would raise up to US$80 billion in stock to fund its AI efforts, with Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway committing US$10 billion.
Investors and analysts will be looking for clues about Microsoft's ongoing plans to pour cash into AI projects during a call with analysts later Wednesday. --AFP

Title: Thousands return home in Spain as new heatwave fuels France wildfires
Article:
ALDEA DEL FRESNO, Spain: Thousands who fled huge wildfires in Spain returned home on Wednesday while in France firefighters battled raging flames as a new heatwave gripped the region.
The neighbouring countries have been gripped by some of the worst forest fires in living memory over the past week, burning vast areas and forcing tens of thousands from their homes.
Spain lifted remaining evacuation orders for Avila province and for the last two towns near Madrid that had been evacuated on Wednesday. While some evacuees returned to untouched homes, others found only devastation.
"I'm happy – I couldn't wait to come home and have my coffee and breakfast," said Maria Jesus Perez Blanca, in her seventies. She was one of about a dozen returnees at the cafes of Aldea del Fresno, west of Madrid on Wednesday morning.
But 12km away in Pelayos de la Presa, David Rodriguez was knocking down the scorched remains of his home.
"It's a disaster. Just look at it," he said. "All my memories, everything I had was here. My dad built it 40 years ago and everything has been lost."
Officials said on Wednesday that better overnight conditions had helped crews stabilise the fire area, and Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez said the coming hours would be "decisive" in the battle to extinguish all the remaining flames.
In France, the Gironde region reported a second calm night and said the massive fire west of France's wine-making capital of Bordeaux remained stable despite a spike in temperatures on Wednesday as the fourth heatwave of the summer roasted the area.
"If the night goes well, we can reasonably be more optimistic for tomorrow and the days to come," Sophie Brocas, a senior regional official, said.
In the southeastern region of Var, however, more than 600 people were forced to flee after a fresh fire erupted in the region nestled along France's Mediterranean coast between the cities of Marseille and Nice.
The new fire erupted less than a day after another blaze in the Var was brought under control.
Another forest fire erupted in the eastern region of Burgundy near the city of Dijon, sweeping across 125 hectares but without causing any casualties or damage to homes, local officials said.
It began in the afternoon in the Combe du Vaulon, a dry valley located in the wine-growing commune of Couchey, about 10km southwest of Dijon.
- EUROPE-WIDE DISASTER -
Europe has been gripped by successive heatwaves and a major drought this year, which scientists have attributed to human-caused climate change.
Extreme heat has parched vegetation that grew vigorously during wet weather earlier in the year, creating tinderbox conditions.
In Spain, 207,000 hectares of land has burned nationwide, among the largest areas in any January to July period on record according to the European Forest Fire Information System. Spanish authorities have reported marginally different figures.
In France, some 92,000 hectares have burned over the same period – the largest area ever documented in records that date back two decades.
While the current focus is on Western Europe, the EU warned this week that fire-prone conditions would spread towards the centre of the continent in the coming days.
Emergency crews were already tackling a blaze on the Greek island of Paros. Two firefighters died fighting fires in Crete and a third near the Peloponnese port of Gytheio.
Fires in Turkiye have already forced the evacuation of hundreds of people around tourist beaches in the south, with hundreds of firefighters tackling the flames.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trump vows to hit Iran hard after attack on US bases in Jordan
Article:
Teheran: US President Donald Trump vowed to hit back hard at Iran after it attacked US bases in Jordan on Wednesday, as the Middle East war reignited and again drew in the Islamic republic's proxies.
The warning came after a lull in the fighting – which had spurred hopes of a return to negotiations – appeared to end, sending oil prices jumping five percent over fears of disruptions to global supplies.
On Wednesday, Saudi Arabia and the United States announced strikes on militant bases in Iraq, while US ally Israel accused Iran-backed Hizbollah of a truce violation.
For two days, the world's biggest oil exporter Saudi Arabia has reported drone attacks targeting crude facilities that it blamed on Iraqi armed groups allied with Teheran.
Iran meanwhile launched missiles at US ally Jordan, with Iranian state media later reporting an American attack near the Islamic republic's border with Iraq.
Trump told Fox News: "We'll be hitting them hard...We are going to beat the 'effing s' out of them."
- 'RESISTANCE' -
Saudi security analyst and researcher Hesham Alghannam told AFP: "Teheran is now using its proxy network to sustain leverage while the diplomatic track absorbs international attention.
Iran's state television, meanwhile, reported a US strike in the Piranshahr border area, after the Fars news agency reported a missile hit an uninhabited area, causing no casualties.
Earlier, Jordan's army said it had intercepted five Iranian missiles, with Iran's Revolutionary Guards saying they had targeted US bases there.
"As long as the threats against the Islamic Republic of Iran continue...the resistance will continue," they added.
On another front, Israel accused Hizbollah of deploying a drone overnight against an Israeli vehicle inside Lebanon, in what the military called "a blatant violation of the ceasefire."
Israel fought alongside the US in the first weeks of the war against Iran, while battling Hizbollah in Lebanon, but it has yet to join the latest round of strikes against the Islamic republic.
- 'DANGEROUS' -
US stocks ended sharply lower on the oil price jump Wednesday, while the yield on 30-year US Treasury bonds hit their highest levels since 2007.
In Iraq, a joint US-Saudi air operation followed attacks by what Riyadh called "militias loyal to Iran" on its oil facilities.
The US military said logistics and weapons sites belonging to an Iran-aligned group were targeted in the strikes.
Iraq's Hashed al-Shaabi alliance said the attacks killed at least 20 of its members.
It denounced a "dangerous escalation" against an "official security institution."
Two Hashed officials said five Iranian advisors were among those killed, and AFP correspondents saw coffins draped with Iranian flags.
The Hashed al-Shaabi alliance, also known as the Popular Mobilisation Forces, was created in 2014 to fight jihadists before its integration into the military.
It includes brigades belonging to Iran-backed groups reputed for acting unilaterally.
Iraq denounced the US-Saudi strikes and said it rejects "all acts of aggression, regardless of the party responsible or the justifications presented."
The Ministerial Council for National Security said it would "confront any violation of Iraq's sovereignty, and prevent any source from using Iraqi territory to threaten neighbouring states."
According to Fox News, however, Trump said the strikes were "coordinated with the Iraqi government."
The strikes follow growing US pressure on Iraq to disarm pro-Iran groups. Earlier this month, Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi visited both the US and Iran.
- RED SEA -
The US had said the days-long cessation in fighting was aimed at kickstarting a new round of negotiations, including over the Strait of Hormuz, which Iran has blockaded throughout much of the war.
The Revolutionary Guards said they had attacked and stopped three tankers in the strait, insisting Iran has "full control" of the waterway that was previously free to transit.
Teheran has insisted it will retain control of the crucial conduit for energy shipments, and has also announced plans to collect fees for passage, which Washington opposes.
The US also announced new sanctions targeting entities linked to Iran's Guards that it accused of extorting ships transiting the strait.
The Hormuz closure has lent greater significance to the Red Sea, Riyadh's alternative export route.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Meta profit falls 14pct as AI spending climbs to US$145bil
Article:
SAN FRANCISCO: Facebook-parent Meta reported profits on Wednesday that fell short of Wall Street expectations, as the cost of staying in the race to deploy artificial intelligence – along with hefty legal and severance charges – hurt its bottom line.
The social media giant said net income dropped 14 per cent from a year earlier to US$15.8 billion.
Revenue, however, climbed 28 per cent to US$60.8 billion, beating estimates and underscoring the continued strength of its advertising business.
Shares in Meta were down as much as 12 per cent in after-hours trading, a sign of analyst skepticism over the scale of the company's AI spending.
Its results contrasted with those of Microsoft, another tech giant that has faced investor doubts but beat analyst expectations on Wednesday, driven by its cloud and artificial intelligence businesses.
At Meta, the profit decline was driven largely by one-time items, including US$2.4 billion in charges tied to legal proceedings and US$1.2 billion in severance from a round of layoffs in May.
Meta has been fighting court and regulatory battles around the world, including one in which a California jury in March ordered Meta and Google to pay US$6 million to a 20-year-old woman who said the platforms had addicted her as a child.
The decision was a first-of-its-kind verdict that could be echoed in thousands of similar cases against Meta still pending.
Meta reaffirmed that it would keep spending heavily on the data centers and chips underpinning its AI effort, telling investors it now expects capital expenditures of US$130 billion to US$145 billion this year – nearly double what it spent in 2025 and slightly higher than its last forecast.
"AI is accelerating our core business today, powering our next generation of products, and opening the door to entirely new enterprise opportunities," chief executive Mark Zuckerberg said in a statement.
- 'MEANINGFUL PREMIUM' -
The new opportunities referred to Meta's plan to launch a cloud computing business that would rent out its vast computing power to outside customers.
"We have quite a number of offers at a meaningful premium over what we paid for the (computing power)," Zuckerberg said on a call to analysts after the earnings report.
This would offer a new revenue stream, echoing a strategy Elon Musk's SpaceX has used to help finance its own AI infrastructure.
Unlike rivals Amazon, Microsoft and Google, Meta has never sold cloud services externally.
Zuckerberg's "optimistic, positive tone" on AI's business possibilities "stands in stark contrast to the negative sentiment that's building toward social media companies over claims that they've harmed and addicted kids," said Emarketer senior analyst Minda Smiley.
"This juxtaposition could make it more difficult for Meta to build credibility in an area where it's already a laggard," Smiley added.
Meta's virtual reality division, Reality Labs, remained deep in the red, posting an operating loss of US$4.6 billion in the quarter.
The unit has bled tens of billions of dollars, and Meta has increasingly shifted its hardware focus toward AI-powered smart glasses, a promising consumer release outside social media.
Unusually for a big tech company, Meta's AI spending spree has seen its cash pile wind down, with free cash flow falling to US$784 million from US$8.5 billion a year earlier.
A similar AI-related cash burn spooked Wall Street last week when Google reported its latest earnings.
Microsoft on Wednesday reported US$90 billion in revenue and US$35.8 billion in net income for its most recently completed quarter, potentially alleviating investor concerns about whether its investments in AI are paying off.
Amazon, a major AI investor, and Apple, which has largely stayed out of the AI investment frenzy, both report on Thursday.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pantun contest returns for 2nd year
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
Following the success of its inaugural edition last year, the Pertandingan Pantun Bertemakan Peribahasa DRB-HICOM Bersama Harian Metro is returning for a second year.
This time, the poetry competition has been expanded to include schools in Negri Sembilan, Melaka and Johor.
Offering a prize of RM45,850, the contest was launched at Balai Berita in Bangsar on Tuesday.
The competition is held in collaboration with Dewan Bahasa dan Pustaka as the official language reference and judging panel, with support from the Education Ministry and state Education Departments.
DRB-HICOM chief communications officer Cairil Irwan Amir said the competition was organised following the encouraging response to its inaugural edition in Selangor last year.
"Last year's pantun competition received a very good response. Based on that, we felt it was something that should be continued.
"Besides elevating our cultural heritage, the competition allows students to be creative, express themselves on stage and try new things. If we don't continue it, who else will?" he said.
Cairil Irwan and Harian Metro group editor Husain Jahit officiated at the ceremony.
Present were Media Prima Bhd News and Current Affairs deputy group managing editor and New Straits Times group editor Farrah Naz Abd Karim, DRB-HICOM group strategic communications general manager Nur Balkish Hood and DBP Language and Literature Development Department director Tuan Abang Haliman Abang Julai.
Husain said the success of last year's competition showed that pantun and the beauty of Malay proverbs continued to resonate with the younger generation.
"The involvement of DBP as the official judging panel further enhances the quality of the competition," he said.
The competition is open to students in Form One to Form Five, except those studying in fully residential schools.
Entries may be submitted between Aug 10 and Aug 31.

Title: HBA: 'No deposit' still carries financial burden
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
KUALA LUMPUR: Affordable housing schemes should not only help Malaysians buy their first home but also ensure they can comfortably repay their loans over the long term.
National House Buyers Association (HBA) secretary-general Datuk Chang Kim Loong said schemes such as Rumah Selangorku and Rumah Mampu Milik had helped first-time buyers overcome one of the biggest barriers — raising the upfront 10 per cent deposit.
"For many, the deposit — not the monthly instalment — is the biggest hurdle. By reducing or eliminating this upfront cost, these schemes have enabled thousands to enter the housing market years earlier than they otherwise could.
"However, affordability should not be measured solely by the ability to obtain the key to a house. It must also include the ability to comfortably service the housing loan over the next 30 to 35 years.
"A buyer who finances 100 per cent of the purchase price will inevitably pay substantially more in total interest than someone who makes a meaningful down payment. The larger the loan, the heavier the long-term financial burden."
Chang said saving for a deposit would foster a buyer's financial discipline, reflecting their commitment to homeownership.
"But when everything is financed through borrowing, there is a risk that some buyers may underestimate the seriousness of the long-term commitment as they have invested little or none of their own money in the initial phase."
Still, Chang said this should not be seen as an argument against such "essential" schemes.
"Deposit assistance should come with financial literacy, prudent lending standards and careful assessment of repayment capacity. The objective should not merely be to help people buy a house today, but to ensure they can sustainably own that home for decades without financial distress."
Without affordable housing schemes, Chang said homeownership would grow harder for young Malaysians in urban areas, where prices had outpaced incomes.
"Ultimately, these schemes are valuable and necessary. However, they should not create the misconception that 'no deposit' means 'no financial burden'.
"The true measure of success is not how easily one can obtain a housing loan, but whether one can repay it comfortably while maintaining a reasonable quality of life," he added.

Title: Top earners make six times more
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
KUALA LUMPUR: The top 10 per cent of formal sector employees earned at least RM11,500 a month in March 2026, more than six times the wages of the country's lowest-paid workers.
The Statistics Department reported that 7.9 per cent of formal employees earned below RM1,700 a month in March 2026, a decrease of two percentage points from the corresponding month last year.
The department said the figures highlight a clear gap between high and low earners.
Despite this, the labour market remained stable, with employment still growing.
The number of formal workers rose 3.8 per cent year-on-year to 7.05 million in March 2026.
Men made up 55 per cent of the workforce and had a median wage of RM3,064, slightly higher than RM3,000 for women.
Workers aged 45 to 49 earned the highest median wages, ranging from RM4,100 to RM4,156 in the first quarter.
All age groups saw wage growth, except workers under 20.
Workers aged 55 to 59 recorded the biggest wage rise, while those under 20 stayed at RM1,700 since February 2025.
Kuala Lumpur had the highest median wage at RM4,527, followed by Selangor (RM3,445) and Penang (RM3,064).
Kelantan, Perlis and Sabah had the lowest median monthly wages, ranging from RM1,827 to RM2,082.
